name: vibebox
description: Universal local-first memory middleware where AI agents provide structured memory candidates and Core manages them.

interface.shortDescription: Local structured memory for AI coding agents.
interface.longDescription: Use VibeBox's local CLI and shared skill instructions to retrieve active guidance before coding, then capture the original userRequest with AI-agent structured memory candidates after work. Pretask always includes active global user-profile baselines even without lexical overlap, while unrelated global technical memory remains relevance-filtered; localized display fields also participate in matching. On first initialization, the agent infers the user's actual conversation language, generates every schema-defined display-template value in that language, and passes the exact canonical BCP 47 tag and template to init. Every reusable memory candidate must also contain displayTitle, displaySummary, and displayRule in that configured language with a matching displayLanguage. VibeBox Core has no hardcoded language packs and rejects missing or mismatched display data instead of silently rendering English. Agents prefer global scope for durable user-centered preferences unless the memory is clearly project-bound. Core does not infer active memory from raw requests or summaries; it validates, stores, dedupes, indexes, links, and renders the candidates supplied by the agent. In Codex App or any sandboxed host, pretask/context are read-only retrieval commands but still require read access to the single global store at <USER_HOME>/.vibebox, %USERPROFILE%\.vibebox, or VIBEBOX_HOME. Aftertask is a global-store write/capture operation and may need write approval for project registration, active memory, indexes, and wiki updates. Run vibebox setup-codex to back up ~/.codex/config.toml and add ~/.vibebox to sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots when the host should avoid repeated approval prompts. If approval is denied, report VibeBox guidance or capture unavailable; do not create workspace-local snapshots, copied stores, project-local .vibebox folders, pointer files, or hidden metadata fallbacks.
defaultPrompt: Before meaningful work in Codex App, check whether VibeBox global store read/write access may need approval.
If Codex repeatedly asks for global-store approval, run or recommend vibebox setup-codex and then restart Codex.

If the global store is missing, infer the user's language from the conversation, run the bundled schema command with --language set to its canonical BCP 47 tag, generate every initialization.displayTemplate value in that language, and pass both to init; never run bare init for a non-English user language.
Resolve the VibeBox plugin root from the loaded skills/vibebox/SKILL.md source, then use node <plugin-root>/bin/vibebox.mjs for every VibeBox command.

Do not probe for a global vibebox.cmd or vibebox command, do not inspect the current project's bin directory, and do not check whether the VibeBox repository was cloned; plugin installation is self-contained.
Generate a VibeBox pre-task brief with the bundled CLI.
Treat global user-profile baselines surfaced by pretask as active guidance even when their lexical match score is zero; do not require a full report scan before normal work.

Before creating any VibeBox candidate file, run the bundled CLI schema --format json, use only the returned schema enums and candidateSkeleton, and write every required display field in schema.configuredMemoryLanguage.
Set displayLanguage to the exact schema.configuredMemoryLanguage value; never copy canonical English text into displayTitle, displaySummary, or displayRule for a user configured in another language.
Never guess memoryRole, type, modelClass, scope, primaryCategory, relatedCategories, confidence, or sourceType; do not invent labels such as project_outcome or project_result.
Prefer scope global for user personal preferences, repeated procedures, tool, validation, and response/reporting preferences unless they are clearly project-bound.
Capture this task with userRequest and structured candidates for each reusable meaning unit.
If global store write approval is denied, report that aftertask capture, project registration, active memory, and wiki updates were not completed.
If one candidate is truly enough, include whyOnlyOneCandidate; if no durable memory exists, submit no_reusable_memory_candidate with noCandidateReason instead of forcing task_context.
Audit VibeBox memory manually when debugging.
